homeowner_setup: Any homeowner, front door, first knock of the roleplay.
goal: Before typing anything, say out loud (or type as a stage direction) your stance: shoulders angled not squared, hands open, smile, then your opener - all inside 3 seconds, before the homeowner's first line lands.
pass_criteria: Kenny states name + HMP + what he sells first (69-1602), in a friendly/curious tone, with no aggressive or authoritative phrasing, before asking anything else.

title_en: One small ask, not the whole job
title_es: Un solo paso, no todo el trabajo
homeowner_setup: Any objection-heavy homeowner (e.g. skeptical-owner or price-shopper).
goal: Never try to close the whole job on the porch. End the exchange asking for exactly one specific next step: a free look, or a named day and time - never 'I'll call you' or a vague 'let me think about it, I'll follow up.'
pass_criteria: The last thing Kenny asks for is one concrete, specific next step with a day/time or a free-look yes/no - not an open-ended promise to circle back.

homeowner_setup: The blunt or annoyed homeowner (existing 40s-annoyed or blunt-60s type).
goal: Homeowner starts short and dismissive. Kenny must stay warm and curious the whole time, never matching their sharpness or sounding authoritative/pushy.
pass_criteria: Homeowner's warmth score improves by the end of the exchange and Kenny's lines contain no commanding/pressuring phrasing ('you need to', 'you have to act now').

homeowner_setup: A homeowner who opens with a flat "not interested, thanks" and starts to close the door.
goal: Kenny gets one more sentence in without being pushy: acknowledge it, then offer the smallest possible ask (a free look, a card) instead of arguing or repeating the same pitch louder.
pass_criteria: Kenny does not repeat his original pitch verbatim, does not argue, and offers exactly one low-pressure next step before accepting a no.

homeowner_setup: No homeowner - solo warmup before the first real roleplay of the session.
goal: Before facing any AI homeowner, type out (as if spoken aloud) the full opener once, from memory, with no notes.
pass_criteria: The typed opener includes name, HMP, and what's being sold, in a natural (not word-for-word script-sounding) way, completed before starting the first homeowner.

title_en: Photos and scope before any signature
title_es: Fotos y alcance antes de firmar nada
homeowner_setup: A homeowner ready to move fast (e.g. the check-in-hand or fast-decision type).
goal: Kenny shows/describes the photo evidence and a real scope of what's damaged before mentioning any paperwork, and is clear about exactly what document is being signed and why (inspection permission vs. contract) - never lets the homeowner think signing something now guarantees a price or a payout.
pass_criteria: Kenny mentions photos/evidence and the specific document's purpose before any signature is discussed, and never implies a signature guarantees insurance payment.

title_en: Say the 3-day cancel right out loud
title_es: Di el derecho de 3 días en voz alta
homeowner_setup: Any homeowner who reaches the paperwork stage of the roleplay.
goal: Kenny must explicitly say (not just mention handing over a form) that the homeowner has 3 days to cancel, in both English and Spanish phrasing, before the roleplay ends.
pass_criteria: Both an English and a Spanish sentence stating the 3-day cancel right appear in Kenny's lines before paperwork is considered done.

title_en: When they ask about the deductible
homeowner_setup: A homeowner who asks directly: "Can you just cover my deductible?" or "Will insurance pay for everything?"
goal: Kenny answers honestly that the deductible is always the homeowner's part and he can't promise what insurance will pay, without sounding evasive or cold.
pass_criteria: Kenny's answer contains no offer, hint or implication of covering/waiving/rebating the deductible and no promise that insurance will pay; tone stays warm, not defensive.

homeowner_setup: A cautious homeowner who asks "What exactly am I signing right now?"
goal: Kenny clearly names which of the three things is being signed at that moment - permission to inspect, a contingency tied to claim approval, or the final job contract - and what it does and doesn't commit the homeowner to.
pass_criteria: Kenny names the specific document type and states in plain words what it commits the homeowner to (or doesn't), with no vague "just paperwork" answer.

homeowner_setup: No homeowner - a reflection prompt shown after 3+ discouraging roleplay results in a row.
goal: Write one line reframing the losses as data (doors knocked vs. interested), not as personal failure, and name the one thing to try differently on the next door.
pass_criteria: The written reflection mentions a ratio or count (not just a feeling) and names one specific change for the next attempt.

title_en: Whose name is on the house?
title_es: ¿A nombre de quién está la casa?
homeowner_setup: A homeowner ready to do paperwork while the spouse is away.
goal: Kenny treats "whose name is on the house?" as a normal paperwork step, so the owner(s) on the title are the ones who sign, and offers a no-pressure way to include a co-owner (a set time to come back, photos to share).
pass_criteria: Kenny asks whose name is on the house (title/deed) or who owns it before any signature, in a calm, normal way, and offers a no-pressure option for a co-owner. FAIL if he pressures with anything like "both spouses must be here or there's no deal" or "the price is only good if you both sign now", or lets someone who is not on the title sign.
